$comment: Facts for the home-page Fact Shuffler (replaces spotifyPlaylists). headline = catchy Doto display line; body = the fact in plain editorial prose; category = small mono label. One is shown at random on load; 'next fact' cycles randomly without repeating until all are seen (tracked in sessionStorage), then resets.

items.headline: The loudest sound in recorded history
items.body: When Krakatoa erupted in 1883, the blast was heard nearly 5,000 km away and circled the globe as a pressure wave — barometers picked it up seven times.

items.headline: A day longer than a year
items.body: Venus spins so slowly that it completes an orbit of the Sun before it finishes a single rotation. Its day is longer than its year.

items.headline: Cleopatra was closer to the Moon landing
items.body: Less time separates Cleopatra from the Apollo 11 landing than from the construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza.

items.headline: Oxford is older than the Aztec Empire
items.body: Teaching at Oxford began around 1096. The Aztec capital of Tenochtitlan wasn't founded until 1325 — two centuries later.

items.headline: The Great Wave is not a painting
items.body: Hokusai's most famous image is a woodblock print — thousands of copies were made and sold cheaply, and its deep blue came from Prussian blue, a pigment imported from Europe.

items.headline: France spans twelve time zones
items.body: Thanks to its overseas territories, France covers more time zones than any other country — more than Russia or the USA.

items.headline: Space smells like seared steak
items.body: Astronauts returning from spacewalks consistently report a scent of hot metal and seared meat clinging to their suits — the byproduct of atomic oxygen.

items.headline: The animal that ages backwards
items.body: The jellyfish Turritopsis dohrnii can revert its adult cells back to their juvenile state, effectively restarting its life cycle — it's biologically immortal.

items.headline: A war shorter than a lunch break
items.body: The Anglo-Zanzibar War of 1896 lasted roughly 38 minutes — the shortest recorded war in history.

items.headline: Saudi Arabia imports camels from Australia
items.body: Australia has the world's largest population of wild dromedary camels — descendants of imported working animals — and exports some of them back to the Middle East.

items.headline: The Night Watch was cropped like a bad thumbnail
items.body: In 1715 Rembrandt's masterpiece was physically trimmed on all four sides — losing two entire figures — just to fit a wall in Amsterdam's town hall.

items.headline: Switzerland can shelter its entire population
items.body: Swiss law long required nuclear shelters for every resident — the country maintains enough bunker capacity for more than its whole population.

items.headline: The Sahara was green
items.body: As recently as 6,000 years ago, the Sahara had lakes, grasslands, hippos and crocodiles. Rock art in its driest corners still shows people swimming.

items.headline: The loneliest place on Earth
items.body: Point Nemo in the Pacific is so far from land that the nearest humans are often astronauts passing overhead on the ISS. Space agencies use it as a spacecraft graveyard.

items.headline: Everyone you know fits in one pixel
items.body: In 1990, Voyager 1 photographed Earth from 6 billion km away. The entire planet occupied less than a single pixel — Carl Sagan's 'pale blue dot'.
